opex.name: Operating costs
opex.note: The day-to-day cost of running the company — people, technology and offices. At 15.0% of revenue (the operating cost ratio, up from 12.4% a year ago), it includes $799M of final cyberattack response costs and restructuring items; the adjusted ratio was 13.5%.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization
opex.note: A non-cash charge spreading the cost of buildings, equipment, software and acquired businesses over their useful lives.

footerNote: Net earnings of $218M include $208M belonging to noncontrolling interests; $10M is attributable to common shareholders — $0.01 per share.

kpis.note: $113.2B in revenue, vs $100.8B a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $5.98 a year ago; adjusted EPS was $2.11

kpis.label: Medical care ratio
kpis.note: Share of premiums paid out as medical care — up from 87.6% a year ago; adjusted ratio was 91.5%

kpis.label: Earnings from operations
kpis.note: UnitedHealthcare $0.3B, Optum $0.1B — down from $7.8B a year ago

oneTimers: A fourth-quarter charge of $2,878M before tax ($1,622M after tax, $1.78 per share): $799M of final direct costs from the 2024 cyberattack, $2,521M of restructuring and other actions — including a $623M reserve for loss-making third-party contracts, $746M for real estate rationalization and workforce reductions, $573M of contract reassessments, $329M of net valuation losses on equity securities and $250M to advance-fund the United Health Foundation — partly offset by $442M of net gains on portfolio divestitures.

Below operating earnings, UnitedHealth booked a $126M loss on the sale of a subsidiary and subsidiaries held for sale, tied to the remaining South American businesses it is exiting as it refocuses on U.S. health care.
The quarter's adjusted EPS of $2.11 (versus $0.01 GAAP) also excludes $386M of intangible amortization; adjusted earnings from operations were $3,132M versus $380M GAAP.
otherDetail: Other expense of $1,100M is $974M of interest expense plus a $126M loss on sale of subsidiary and subsidiaries held for sale (mainly the remaining South American businesses). Investment income is not in this line — it is already counted in revenue. The $938M tax line is a benefit, not a charge: the quarter lost $720M before tax, so taxes added $938M back to net earnings.

segments.name: Premiums
segments.note: Health-insurance premiums from members, employers and government programs — the money people pay for coverage. UnitedHealthcare served 49.8 million people in the quarter, and Medicare & Retirement revenue grew sharply on Inflation Reduction Act Part D changes.

segments.name: Products
segments.note: Prescription drugs and other products sold, mainly through Optum Rx pharmacies.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Fees for delivering care and for health technology and data services, mainly from Optum Health clinics and Optum Insight.

segments.name: Investment and other income
segments.note: Income from the company's investment portfolio and other small sources — down sharply from $1.6B a year ago.

takeaways.text: The medical care ratio — the share of premiums paid out as medical care — jumped to 92.4%, from 87.6% a year ago, as Medicare funding cuts, Inflation Reduction Act changes and accelerating cost trends outran premium increases. Even stripping out the quarter's charge, the adjusted ratio was 91.5%. Medical costs of $82.0B left only $18.5B of gross profit on $113.2B of revenue.
takeaways.title: Medical costs ate almost everything

takeaways.text: UnitedHealth booked a $2,878M pre-tax charge: $799M of final cyberattack costs and $2,521M of restructuring and other actions — including a $623M reserve for loss-making contracts, $746M for real estate and workforce cuts and $329M of investment valuation losses — partly offset by $442M of divestiture gains. Optum Health swung to a $2,783M operating loss; Optum Rx was the one bright spot, earning $2,885M, up from $1,739M.
takeaways.title: A one-time charge crushed the quarter

takeaways.text: UnitedHealth guided 2026 revenue above $439B — a planned ~2% decline as it sheds members and right-sizes Optum Health — with earnings from operations above $24B and adjusted earnings above $17.75 a share. The medical care ratio is expected to improve to 88.8%. Cash flow from operations was $19.7B in 2025, 1.5 times net income.
takeaways.title: 2026 outlook: smaller, more profitable

verdict: UnitedHealth Group's revenue grew 12% to $113.2B, but a 92.4% medical care ratio and a $2.9 billion one-time charge left operating profit at just $0.4B and earnings at a penny a share.
